\section{Introduction to the Functional View}
The Functional View describes the functional elements of the system, their responsibilities, interfaces, and primary interactions.

\section{Core Architectural Elements of the Functional View}

\subsection{Overview of Functional Structure}

\subsection{Functional Elements and Responsibilities}


\subsubsection{Game System}
The Game System provides the core gameplay functionality, managing game logic and processing for different cognitive tests.

\textbf{Responsibilities:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item Implement game logic for various cognitive tests (Reaction Time Test, Reflex Test, etc.)
    \item Control game flow and state transitions
    \item Generate stimuli for users to respond to (e.g. targets)
    \item Measure and record user response times and accuracy
    \item Provide interfaces for starting, executing, and ending game sessions
    \item Calculate performance metrics for user responses
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Interfaces:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textit{GameExecution}: Supports the running of different game types, starting the game and allows for the user to interact with the game and its systems.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Multiplayer System}
The Multiplayer System enables real-time competition between multiple users.

\textbf{Responsibilities:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item Manage game rooms for multiplayer sessions
    \item Support room creation with public/private visibility options
    \item Handle player joining and leaving functionality
    \item Synchronize gameplay across multiple participants
    \item Coordinate round-based gameplay and results
    \item Interface with Real-time Communication System for player interactions
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Interfaces:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textit{CommunicationIntegration}: Interfaces with Real-time Communication System as not all messages recieved in the Multiplayer system are room messages.
    \item \textit{Room Management}: Allows users to join or create a game and use Room-level functionality.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Real-time Communication System}
The Real-time Communication System enables instant updates and interactions between system components and users.

\textbf{Responsibilities:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item Handle real-time message passing between system components
    \item Provide reliable message delivery mechanisms
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Interfaces:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textit{MessageDistribution}: Routes messages to appropriate recipients
\end{itemize}

\subsection{External Interfaces}

The Human Benchmark system interacts with several external entities:

\subsubsection{Web Browsers}
The primary means for users to access and interact with the system.


\subsubsection{Database}
The primary means for users to access the system.

\textbf{Interface characteristics:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textit{Save to Database}: Allows various data to be saved in a non-volatile environment.

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Key Interactions and Scenarios}

The key interaction of our change is that Users will have the ability to join/create various chat-rooms and send various messages among them to all users in that chat-room.

\section{Perspective Priorities for the Functional View}

The table below identifies the priority of different architectural perspectives for the Functional View of the Human Benchmark system, which will guide architectural decision-making.

\begin{table}[H]
    \centering
    \caption{Perspective Priorities for the Functional View of Human Benchmark}
    \label{tab:perspective_priorities_functional}
    \begin{tabular}{p{0.3\textwidth}p{0.15\textwidth}p{0.45\textwidth}}
        % \toprule
        \textbf{Architectural Perspective} & \textbf{Priority} & \textbf{Explanation}                                                                                                                                                                                                      \\
        % \midrule
        Performance and Scalability        & High              &  Performance is highly important as due to the nature of chatting, this feature is likely to be one of the most intensly used feature. As such it is very important that this feature remains functional as the number of users increase.   \\

        Security                           & Low              & Since the messages have no connection to a users personal date stored in their account, the importance of security is not important for this change.\\

        Usability                          & High              & The system's success depends on user engagement. The Functional View must ensure that users are able to easily use the chatting feature.                                         \\

        Availability and Resilience        & Medium            & While not life-critical, the system should be consistently available.                \\

        Evolution                          & Low            & Since the main goal of the system is to develop users reaction speeds, and since messages are mainly compromised only of text there is little need for change.                                                                \\

        Development Resource               & Medium            & The functional elements should be designed with implementation efficiency in mind, aligning with the modern tech stack while minimizing unnecessary complexity for the development team.                                               \\

        Internationalization               & Low               & While the system may eventually be used globally, the functional capabilities of cognitive tests are largely language-independent. Only user interface elements would require adaptation.                                                                    \\

        Accessibility                      & Low               & Basic input accessibility concerns exist, but the nature of reaction time tests inherently requires certain motor and visual capabilities.                                                         \\

        Location                           & Low               & The system is web-based without significant geographical dependencies. The only minor concerns might be latency considerations for multiplayer scenarios across large distances.                                                                                 \\

        Regulation                         & Low               & Beyond standard data protection concerns (handled by the Security perspective), the system doesn't operate in a highly regulated domain like finance or healthcare.                                                                                          \\
        % \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\section{Impact of Key Perspectives on the Functional View}

Based on the priorities identified, the following perspective has the most significant impact on the Functional View of the system: The Real-time Communication System must be designed for low-latency message passing, with optimized protocols for multiplayer synchronization that can accommodate up to 200 concurrent users without degradation.


\section{Importance and Justification of the Functional View for Human Benchmark}

The Functional View is critically important for the Human Benchmark system for several key reasons:

\subsection{Core Purpose Alignment}


\begin{itemize}
    \item Allow users to chat globally, in game rooms, in group chats and privately.
    \item Allow to create join and leave group chats and private messages
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Stakeholder Communication}

The Functional View serves as an essential communication tool:

\begin{itemize}
    \item For developers, it provides clear guidance on the system's major functional components and their interfaces, forming the foundation for implementation.
    \item For testers, it establishes the expected behavior and interactions that must be validated.
    \item For acquirers and users, it clarifies what capabilities the system will provide without delving into technical implementation details.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Quality Attribute Support}

The Functional View shows critical quality attributes for the system:

\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Performance and Scalability:} By clearly defining the Real-time Communications System's need to serve large amounts of users and remain functional developers can prioratise the performance of the new feature.

    \item \textbf{Reliability:} Clear interface definitions between elements enable robust error handling and rigorous testing.


\end{itemize}

\subsection{Architectural Guidance}

The Functional View provides crucial guidance for architectural decisions:

\begin{itemize}
    \item It shows the boundaries and responsibilities of the main system components, guiding implementation.
    \item It describes the main interfaces that must be used, making the development requirements more clear.
\end{itemize}
